verdict.rationale: Requesty documents gateway routing policies that switch models automatically. Fallback policies cover availability by retrying the next model in a chain on timeouts, rate limits, or errors. Weighted load balancing and latency-based routing add further policy options. No documented routing rule selects models by cost or by task capability, and spend caps limit spending rather than route requests. missing for 10: cost-based routing rules, capability-based routing rules, explicit mid-task agent model switching, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can switch models mid-task by policy — cost, capability, or availability — through gateway routing rules

citations.quote: Fallback Policies automatically retry your requests with different models if one fails
If it fails (timeout, rate limit, error, etc.), the router immediately tries the next model in the chain.
Load Balancing Policies distribute your requests across multiple models based on weights you define.
Latency-Based Routing automatically selects the fastest model for each request based on real-time performance data.
